entries.title: BrightAI, which uses AI to help industrial companies detect malfunctioning equipment, raised $97M led by Smith Point, bringing its total funding to $184M (Maria Deutscher/SiliconANGLE)
Asian tech stocks plunge as Anthropic's record IPO fails to stem an AI sell-off; SoftBank falls ~15%, TSMC falls 5%+, and Samsung and SK Hynix fall 6%+ (William Sandlund/Financial Times)
Anthropic fell ~5% in after-hours trading on its debut day, following a record $107.3B IPO (Bloomberg)
California's AG subpoenas Nvidia to investigate whether Jensen Huang's actions resulted in China getting advanced chips, and whether Nvidia misled investors (Katie Nicora/CBS News)
Docs: as of May 2026, the US Commerce Dept. approved sales of 879K+ AI chips to Chinese companies, including entities on the DOD's Chinese military-linked list (CNBC)
Source: National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross was "fired" from his role; the president "fully supported" the firing days after a wave of tech-related outages (Courtney Rozen/Reuters)
Google DeepMind researchers argue AI development is on pace to move beyond human-level AGI to ASI, which consistently outperforms groups of human experts (Tim Genewein/DeepMind Institute)
Source: Iconiq invested more than $6B in Anthropic; its estimated 1.8% stake was worth ~$31.8B at Thursday's close, a 430%+ return on investment (Richard Nieva/Forbes)
Sources: Menlo invested $1B+ for a ~1.5% Anthropic stake, worth $20B+ at a $1.5T valuation; Lightspeed, the top financial investor, invested $3B+ and holds 2%+ (Krystal Hu/Reuters)
Sources: Nvidia is in advanced talks to acquire diffusion LLM developer Inception for $500M+ plus earnouts; talks began before Jensen Huang's resignation (The Information)
Sources: the White House named DOD Chief Information Officer Kirsten A. Davies as its national cyber director, replacing Sean Cairncross who is stepping down (Axios)
A job listing shows Apple is developing an AI agent that can write code, browse the web, control apps, navigate devices, and coordinate subagents for users (Mark Gurman/Bloomberg)
Intuit agrees to sell marketing subsidiary Mailchimp to Bending Spoons for $3.68B in cash and stock; Intuit paid $12B to buy Mailchimp in 2021 (Jordan Novet/CNBC)
At a Senate hearing, Trump's CISA director nominee Michael LoSapio dodged questions about the agency's priorities, denied January 6 was an attack, and more (Eric Geller/Cybersecurity Dive)
Source: Meta plans to charge $300 for its forthcoming Muse Charm device and include a free 5G data plan from Verizon for up to 12 months (Jyoti Mann/The Information)
